note: The generic characters are a rediagnosis for the New Guinean group; the full description is in Miller 1991.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Soldier with a well-developed frontal projection and without lateral tubercles; tibial spur formula 3:2:2 or 2:2:2; worker monomorphic; worker left mandible index usually greater than 1, sometimes slightly lower; enteric valve cushions of two sizes, arranged with threefold radial symmetry, with numerous small triangular spines; worker hindgut P3 divided into 3 portions, small–large–small in that order. It differs from Termes in that the soldier labrum is never drawn out into a slender pointed tip but is always relatively small, with a short point or without a distinct point; the head capsule is proportionally broader; and the mandibles are more strongly curved dorsoventrally.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Frontal projection well developed, without lateral tubercles; labrum relatively small, with a short point or without a distinct point, never drawn out into a slender tip; head capsule proportionally broad; mandibles more strongly curved dorsoventrally; tibial spur formula 3:2:2 or 2:2:2.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Monomorphic. Left mandible index usually greater than 1, sometimes slightly lower; hindgut P3 divided into 3 portions, small–large–small in that order; enteric valve cushions of two sizes, arranged with threefold radial symmetry, with numerous small triangular spines.
